chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the testimony of the father for his son, and of the son for his father, and of the brother for his brother, so he said: It is allowed.
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of a father for his son or a brother for his brother valid in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) affirming the validity of testimony between close male relatives, a ruling that counters the general principle of *'illat* (defect) often applied to kin due to potential bias. This ruling is particularly significant in Shia jurisprudence as it demonstrates the Imam's authority to establish specific evidentiary standards distinct from broader Sunni schools, emphasizing that familial closeness does not inherently invalidate legal testimony.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(The narrator) says,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the testimony of the father for his son, and of the son for his father, and of the brother for his brother. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allowed’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about the testimony of a father for his son, the testimony of a son for his father and the testimony of a brother for his brother. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is permissible.’”
